# Evaluation in Practice {#sec-eng-eval}

Evaluation is how you decide whether a model is good enough to ship and
whether a change made things better or worse. This chapter treats it as
infrastructure: a harness you run continuously, with results you can trust
and act on.

By the end you will be able to build a reproducible evaluation harness,
choose metrics that track what you care about, and run a model comparison
that survives scrutiny.

## What you are measuring

Separating capability from product quality, offline metrics from online
outcomes, and aligning the number you optimize with the outcome you want.

## Building an evaluation harness

Datasets and splits, deterministic runs, versioned prompts and graders,
and making an evaluation cheap enough to run on every change.

## Model-graded and automated evaluation

Using a model as a judge, its biases and failure modes, and calibrating
automated scores against human judgment.

## Human evaluation

Annotation protocols, inter-rater agreement, pairwise preference, and the
cost and latency of putting people in the loop.

## Online evaluation

A/B tests, guardrail metrics, interleaving, and detecting regressions in
production before users do.

## Regression and drift

Continuous evaluation in CI, catching quality regressions across releases,
and noticing when the input distribution has moved.
